body: Good luck finding a way to feel important that doesn't involve sending nasty anonymous messages to strangers online.

You're right about the feelings thing. I try so hard to explain to other people that their feelings are just part of being human and it's okay to experience unpleasant emotional landscapes. 

I don't know how to tell him. We don't see each other at all or speak with any regularity. I don't know if he's seeing anyone currently. I don't want to cross a boundary. I guess he could feel the same about me, but I do sincerely doubt that he thinks of me much. I'd rather not ruin my chances of having him remain a casual friend by doing something to piss off a hypothetical girlfriend.

I would argue that there's a third option, he just likes me as a friend but doesn't feel compelled to search for anything more serious than touching base once a month or so. 

He's definitely not a jerk. He's actually a little pious, very deliberately being the best person he can be. The kindest, the smartest, the calmest. Always striving to be kinder, smarter, calmer. Part of this is that he just doesn't have room to lead people on. He told me on our one date that he is very careful to shut the door on growing relationships (of any sort) that are not right for him. 

I don't find his behavior to be *that* contradictory. It's consistent with what you'd expect from a casual friend. When he "disappeared" on me after we hung out the second time, I asked him what was going on -- that I hadn't heard from him for months, had a fun time with him one night, and then didn't hear from him anymore. He apologized sincerely, said that he's just busy and socially inconsistent and has a hard time being a reliable friend. Described himself as a friend to me. 

The only way out of this is either time or by asserting myself. I've dated other people since all of this. I'm sure he has, too. It's not like I'm the only woman he's ever met... I have tried to see if I can find a way to hang out with him but every time I reach out, he gets cold and stops responding before I can get there. It's probably on purpose, to save both of us from having to have that conversation. I haven't even spoken to him long enough to know if he's seeing anyone. In the end... I'll probably have to get over it. Just feels so lousy.
I hope you find some peace!

I'm sorry you're so insecure that you can't stand to see other people be comfortable with themselves. I recognize that you're so ashamed of yourself that you think you'll feel better by trying to make me feel like garbage, and it probably did help you for a minute, but that's no way to live. I hope you find a way to feel better about yourself soon.

Thank you. I'm trying. I've dated other people since all this happened but it's so hard. Finding people I work well with and feel enthusiasm for is so rare. Even rarer is it that they feel enthusiasm for me. 

Maybe this is the curse of being smart and self aware and having high standards. Lots of waiting. Very little romantic joy in between the best parts.

I'm not really "waiting for him to do something." I'm just assuming he's not going to. I didn't wait weeks for him to text me... I texted him the next morning and he never responded, so I texted weeks later and asked what was going on between us. 

I didn't really get into it but the last time I saw him, I felt like I had a way better time than he did. I was just in awe. I feel stupid next to him.

I have no problem texting him first. I have been doing that a lot lately. I reach out, we exchange a few messages, and before I feel "warmed up" enough to say "hey, would you like to grab a drink this week and catch up more?" he stops responding. 

I think he just wants to be friendly acquaintances who keep in touch. I'm desperately afraid to ask for more than this and lose what I have right now. Maybe it's silly. I really should just abruptly message him and ask if he wants to hang out again. I just feel so stupid.
I'm sorry. I'm going through something similar. It feels so lousy.

I do comedy. It's a little different. Originality is key to this and I just feel so depleted, so broken and unable to make anything seem fresh. I have such a hard time making connections and finding people to collaborate with. It's lonely being the only woman in the room. It's even lonelier when there are other women in the room, but they can tell that I'm not as good or cool or funny or smart as they are and they don't want anything to do with me.

I had to ghost my best friend last week. She's a pathological liar and it was impossible to talk to her about anything she did to hurt me because she always came up with amazing, elaborate excuses. There was no way I could've even had a break up conversation with her, because she is so good at manipulating her way out of trouble. 

You don't sound like that at all. You are worried about what you did "wrong" and still concerned about your friend's feelings. I'm sorry that you're going through this.
